Subject: Comp band schematic & local benchmarks — alignment needed

Hi team,

I attached the latest comp band schematic (comp_band_schema_v2.xlsx) and the regional benchmarking pack (regional_benchmarks_q1-27.pdf). We need a short alignment to lock the guidance we send to hiring managers this week. Key asks: 

- Confirm leveling clarifications between Software Eng IC4/IC5 (we had ambiguity around IC4 senior vs IC5 entry).
- Approve geo multipliers for APAC cluster (IN/SG/AU split) and EMEA core markets.
- Decide whether to adopt a $ cap on offers that are above 1.4x local median for enterprise hires.

Quick context: benchmarking draws from Q1 vendor data and our closed offers for the last 6 months. The spreadsheet includes a proposed Market Index multiplier column (col H) and proposed lower/upper offer caps (col J/K). If we don't finalize by end of day Friday (4/16), hiring will default to current guidance which is inconsistently applied.

Please reply with SC's (Strongly concur) / OK / Needs change on each of the three bullets. If you have precise multiplier suggestions, add them inline in the sheet and flag cells with comments.

Thanks —
Alex

Alex — thanks for pulling this together. Quick readthrough and comments inline, high level:

1) Leveling: Needs change. The current IC4 description still implies ownership of mid-sized projects; IC5 language should be clarified to require cross-team product leadership. I'll insert a short paragraph in the "leveling_notes" tab.

2) Geo multipliers: OK for EMEA core (UK/DE/FR) at +1.15 market index. For APAC, split suggests +1.05 for SG, +0.90 for IN, +1.25 for AU. Those are draft but align with latest offers.

3) Offer cap at 1.4x median — Needs change. For senior/strategic hires (principal/lead), we should allow exceptions if hiring manager gets pre-approval from finance + recruitment lead. Propose an approval flow instead of a hard cap (see approval_matrix.xlsx).

I can join a quick sync if helpful — 2pm PT today open for me.

Laura

All — adding a few operational guardrails from the product/eng viewpoint:

- For IC4 vs IC5, suggest we tie the distinction to two quantifiable signals in the job template: 1) scope (# teams impacted / cross-functional projects) and 2) expected mentorship load (# of reports or hiring mentorship). This makes approvals less subjective.
- Geo multipliers: concur with Laura's splits. For clarity, add a small footnote that SG premiums apply only to remote-hybrid hires where candidate is physically in SG.
- Offer caps: propose a two-tier approval matrix: up to 1.4x — automatic with recruiter + hiring manager signoff; 1.4-1.6x — people ops + finance approval; >1.6x — exec signoff (VP+). That reduces back-and-forth and keeps strategic flexibility.

I'll add the approval_matrix.xlsx draft into the Drive link and flag the relevant rows in the comp_sheet.

-Vivek

Thanks for the ping — reviewed the proposed multipliers and the short answer: no material payroll tax delta that prevents us from proceeding, but two notes: 

1) India (IN): For candidates paid in INR, we need to reflect statutory bonuses and variable in a way that does not exceed local statutory caps on PF/ESI base calculations. I flagged recommended language in the comp sheet comments.
2) Australia (AU): For higher bands with >1.25 multiplier, check superannuation baselines and make sure total cash + equity illustration accounts for employer contribution.

On the approval flow: finance is comfortable with the two-tier approach Vivek outlined, but requests that the 1.4-1.6x tier require a short justification template (1-2 bullets) logged in the candidate ATS record (Doc link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C). We'll draft a one-page justification template and circulate this afternoon.

Decision summary (for comms to hiring managers):
- Leveling: update IC4/IC5 language with objective signals (scope + mentorship) — Laura to edit.
- Geo multipliers: adopt Laura's APAC/EMEA splits; SG premium applies when candidate located in SG.
- Offer caps/approvals: implement Vivek's two-tier matrix; require short justification for 1.4-1.6x; >1.6x escalate to VP.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Reward & Payroll | Redwood Inference
